closed_lines: execution-supervision SFT (12% and 25%/58% composite): mechanism gates failed
execution-feedback repair at inference: C - B Kill@8 +0.38 pp [-1.07, +1.77], FAIL
decision_memo.recommendation: primary: independently constructed repository-native evaluation; secondary (optional): a controlled train-derived sampling-budget study
rationale: every result so far is train-derived or on previously inspected panels; the project cannot currently make any held-out claim, and its only locked test split was consumed

the tool-assisted pilot's only material effect was secondary and unmatched (B - A Kill@8 +6.44 pp from 16 samples plus text-only de-duplicating selection); whether that is real is a cheap, separable question
repository-native execution is the evaluation the research plan actually asks for and has never been demonstrated for generated tests (0 generated tests run natively; official-test reproduction 3/5)
not_recommended: any further execution-supervision or execution-feedback variant (both closed by frozen gates)
reusing the consumed test split or opening the reserved confirmation lineages for a different question
decision_memo.claim_scope: disjointness is enforced against the complete indexed source universe under the recorded repository, fork, commit, patch, issue, and function-similarity checks; this is not a claim that no model has seen these repositories

repository_native_protocol.status: draft; no candidate mined, no split created

candidate_sources.strategy: independently mined bug-fix commits from permissively licensed, pure-Python, pytest-tested GitHub repositories outside the exclusion universe, with fixes merged on or after 2025-01-01
candidate_sources.temporal_rule: fix commit authored and merged on or after 2025-01-01, after the Qwen2.5-Coder release. This is contamination-risk MITIGATION only: it does not show that the model has never seen the repository, the buggy code or a similar fix, and it is never described as proof

not_used_and_why.BugsInPy: all 17 projects are in the exclusion universe
not_used_and_why.SWE-bench / SWE-bench Verified: same 12 repositories; in the exclusion universe
not_used_and_why.HumanEvalFix / HumanEvalPack / EvalPlus: derived from HumanEval/MBPP; near-duplicate by construction
not_used_and_why.Defectors, PyTraceBugs and similar aggre: project overlap with BugsInPy (pandas, ansible, ...) must be screened repository by repository; not used wholesale
not_used_and_why.SWE-rebench / SWE-Gym style collections: admissible only per repository after the same screening, licence review and temporal rule; treated as a candidate index, never as a pre-built split

candidate_sources.screening_note: names only; licence, activity, test suite, Python support and 2025+ bug-fix supply are verified during mining, never assumed. Repositories in the same organisation as an excluded repository (for example pallets, pylint-dev, pytest-dev, psf) are flagged for an explicit decision rather than silently admitted

isolation_rules.claim: disjointness is enforced against the complete indexed source universe under the recorded repository, fork, commit, patch, issue, and function-similarity checks; this is not a claim that no model has seen these repositories
mandatory_evidence: verified https://github.com/<owner>/<name> URL and numeric repository identity
explicit fork status: not_fork, or fork with verified parent owner/name and numeric parent identity
parseable target function with at least 12 comparison shingles
issue or PR identity owner/name#number in the same repository
licence SPDX identifier from the admitted list and the SHA-256 of the licence file
isolation_rules.fail_closed: any missing, unknown or malformed evidence refuses with insufficient_isolation_evidence; nothing defaults to admission
isolation_rules.repository: owner/name, bare name and verified fork parent outside the universe; same-organisation repositories are flagged for decision D2
isolation_rules.issue: issue/PR identifier not a known benchmark instance
isolation_rules.patch_lineage: commits not known benchmark commits; normalised patch not identical to, and Jaccard < 0.80 against, every indexed BugsInPy and SWE-bench Verified patch
isolation_rules.function_lineage: target function Jaccard < 0.80 against every indexed reference function; nearest match, score and fingerprint recorded
isolation_rules.within_set: one target per fix commit and function lineage; pairwise near-duplicate check within the new set
isolation_rules.coverage: audit_source_coverage requires concrete indexed counts and bound input files for every corpus source and for the train view and legacy real-bug files; an unknown, unindexed or zero-count source fails
isolation_rules.receipt: every isolation record carries the SHA-256 of results/v4_3_reference_universe_receipt.json; a record made against any other universe is invalid and must be recomputed

licensing_and_reproducibility.licence_evidence: SPDX identifier from the repository LICENSE file at the buggy commit, recorded with its hash
licensing_and_reproducibility.checkout: full clone (no blob-less partial clone: the existing ingestion cache is unusable for checkouts); buggy and fixed commits recorded by SHA; tree hashes stored
licensing_and_reproducibility.python_versions: 3.8, 3.9, 3.11 and 3.12 are available in WSL today; 3.10 and 3.13 need an approved installer; each bug uses the lowest supported version declared by the project at that commit
licensing_and_reproducibility.dependencies: one dependency environment per target, shared by the buggy and the fixed revision: dependencies are resolved ONCE from the declared requirements of both revisions into a hash-pinned lock (uv pip compile --generate-hashes, or pip-compile --generate-hashes) and installed with hash checking (uv pip sync / pip install --require-hashes). The project itself is not installed into the environment; each revision's checkout is placed on the path (and rebuilt in place if it has compiled parts) when its tests run. pip freeze is not used as a lock: it records versions without hashes
licensing_and_reproducibility.environment_evidence: interpreter version, lock file and its SHA-256, resolver and version, install log hash, WSL distribution, kernel and CPU count per environment
licensing_and_reproducibility.shared_environment_rule: if no single lock satisfies both revisions' declared requirements, or either revision cannot import or build against the shared lock, the target is disqualified before evaluation. No per-revision environments are used unless a separate rule is predeclared and approved

steps: build environments for the buggy and the fixed revision
run the official regression test (or an independently written and reviewed test, recorded as such) three times on each revision
qualify only if it fails 3/3 on buggy and passes 3/3 on fixed with identical environment locks
inject generated tests into both revisions under an isolated file name; run each with a per-test timeout; repeat any discordant result once to detect flakiness

outcome_classes.semantic_kill: fails on buggy by assertion, passes on fixed
outcome_classes.crash_kill: fails on buggy by an uncaught exception from project code, passes on fixed
outcome_classes.timeout_on_buggy: times out on buggy, passes on fixed; reported separately, never merged into semantic kills
outcome_classes.harness_failure: collection error, injection error, pytest internal error
outcome_classes.dependency_failure: import of a missing or incompatible package

native_qualification.infrastructure_rule: harness, dependency and environment failures are never counted as kills or as model failures; they are excluded from denominators, reported with counts, and a target with any environment failure on either revision is disqualified before evaluation, not after

permitted: its signature, type hints and docstring
buggy-side module-level context needed to call it (imports, constants, class definition skeletons)
public documentation strings present at the buggy commit
forbidden: issue or PR discussion describing the fix
context_policy.enforcement: prompt built from a permitted view, as in the tool-assisted loop; a leakage scan over every prompt for any line of the fixed function, patch or official test; the prompt-from-view equality check is repeated

target_size.basis: results/v4_3_repository_native_power_analysis.json: under the frozen +5 pp gate the 80%-power minimum detectable paired Kill@8 effect is about 11.8 pp at N=100, 10.1 at 150, 9.2 at 200 and 8.1 at 300 (discordance 0.21, rho 0.05, 25 repositories); the gate is not changed to fit the sample

composition.unit: one target function per unique bug; unique function lineages and fix commits
composition.tiers: simple, moderate and complex all present; minimum 20% each where supply allows, otherwise the shortfall is reported, never filled by repetition
composition.no_repetition_balancing: no duplicated targets, no resampling to balance; exact unique counts and every exclusion with its reason are reported
composition.rehearsal_pool: a separate pool of 20-30 qualified bugs from at least 5 repositories that are never admitted to the final set, used only for the dress rehearsal

atheris_protocol.tool: actual atheris 2.3.0 (libFuzzer) under WSL Python 3.11; never the simulated baseline.coverage_fuzzer, which is reported under its own name if at all
atheris_protocol.eligibility: a target is Atheris-applicable if the adapter can construct well-typed arguments that reach the target function; applicability and ineligibility counts are reported separately, with reasons. An ineligible target is never recorded as a tested zero
atheris_protocol.oracle: identical buggy/fixed revisions for both systems
atheris_protocol.adapter: strongest reasonable structured-input adapter: type-hint and docstring driven, full-range integers and floats, bytes, nested containers, dict/set/tuple, dataclass/NamedTuple construction, and seeds from literals in the buggy function; reachability of the defect is reported per target

budgets.oneiros_budget: 8 candidates per target, reported as model calls, tokens, GPU seconds and CPU execution seconds
budgets.note: budgets differ in kind; both are reported explicitly and no single 'equal budget' claim is made

atheris_protocol.reporting: crash kills and semantic kills separately; kills per CPU-second; per-seed and seed-aggregated results

modes.ordinary_crash_contract: fuzzes the buggy function alone; a finding is an uncaught exception or a violated declared contract (annotated types, documented preconditions); it counts as a kill only if the same input replayed on the fixed revision does not fail
modes.differential_oracle: fixed and buggy run side by side; any divergence is a finding. Reported separately and labelled a generous upper bound, because Oneiros never receives the fixed implementation

atheris_protocol.primary_comparison: Oneiros versus ordinary crash/contract Atheris, paired by target, on the jointly eligible set only

dress_rehearsal.data: the rehearsal pool only (never the final set)
stages: analysis on rehearsal data with the frozen analysis code
dress_rehearsal.gate: every stage completes with receipts and zero unexplained failures before any one-time evaluation is requested

secondary: semantic kills and crash kills separately
reference validity (passes on fixed) per requested candidate
slices by complexity tier, bug family and repository

repository-stratified performance and repository-cluster sensitivity (the paired estimate recomputed with each repository dropped); this is not leave-one-repository-out generalisation, which would need retraining
ordinary and differential Atheris kills, applicability counts, kills per CPU-second
metrics.intervals: Wilson 95% for single proportions; paired comparisons by exact McNemar and a repository-cluster bootstrap 90% interval (10,000 replicates, fixed seed)
comparisons: Oneiros vs ordinary Atheris on the jointly eligible set (paired, primary Atheris comparison)
differential-oracle Atheris reported as a labelled upper bound
metrics.decision_rules: predeclared before the one-time run: a model comparison passes only with a +5 pp Kill@8 gain and cluster-bootstrap lower bound > 0, reference validity within -3 pp; everything else is reported descriptively; no configuration is selected on the final set

per_run: execution logs, return codes, timeouts and durations for both revisions
Atheris logs, corpora sizes, coverage and seeds
WSL distribution, kernel, CPU and memory
receipts.rollback: no artifact is overwritten; a failed run is preserved and marked invalid; the one-time set is sealed by hash before any model sees it and is never re-evaluated after a protocol change

sampling_budget_protocol.question: Does generating sixteen candidates and keeping eight by text-only selection improve Kill@8 over the first eight, at twice the generation cost?

panel_options.recommended: the 613-record retention panel with a fresh seed family (seed 43), exploratory; its canonical seed-42 Kill@8 for the control is already known (0.633), which is disclosed
panel_options.rejected: the 264-record tool-assisted panel: its B - A comparison (+6.44 pp) is already observed, so a study there would be post hoc

arms.S8: the first eight of sixteen samples drawn in one call (current policy's eight)
arms.S16_select8: all sixteen from the same call, then the frozen text-only policy: parser/policy-valid, first-occurrence non-duplicates in generation order, first eight

sampling_budget_protocol.cost_accounting: S16 costs twice the generated sequences of S8; generated tokens, GPU seconds and wall time are reported for both; the comparison is framed as 'more samples plus selection', not as a free gain
sampling_budget_protocol.gate: S16_select8 - S8 Kill@8 >= +5 pp with cluster-bootstrap 90% lower bound > 0 and reference validity within -3 pp; otherwise inconclusive or fail; exploratory either way

frozen_details.generation: one generate call per record with num_return_sequences=16, seed derived_seed(43, record_id, 's16') applied immediately before the call, unchanged successor settings otherwise
frozen_details.candidate_ordering: the 16 sequences in the order the call returns them (index 0-15)
frozen_details.s8: sequences 0-7 exactly, in order; the analysis verifies byte-identical raw outputs and hashes against sequences 0-7 of the S16 record (nested arm)
frozen_details.validity: a candidate is valid if the frozen whole-output parser accepts it (parse and candidate policy); nothing is executed for selection
frozen_details.duplicate_definition: whitespace-collapsed normalised code (harness.execution_feedback.normalised_code) equal to an EARLIER valid candidate
frozen_details.selection: walk indices 0-15; keep valid first occurrences in order until eight are kept
frozen_details.fewer_than_eight: fill the remaining slots with the not-kept candidates (invalid or duplicate) in ascending index order; always exactly eight slots
frozen_details.implementation: harness.tool_assisted_generation.select_final with slot=index and round=1, whose policy is exactly this rule
frozen_details.difference_from_canonical: S8 is the first eight of a 16-sample call, not the canonical 8-sample batch-of-2 protocol; the study compares S8 and S16->8 with each other only

assumptions.mining_funnel: yield 7-15% from mined candidate fix commits to qualified single-function targets; N=300 needs about 2,000-4,300 candidates (3,000 at 10%)

environment_build.storage_gb: about 90 kept (300 x 0.3), up to 270 before pruning

qualification.wall_hours: about 4 (900 x 2 revisions x 3 repeats x 45 s / 16)

one_time_evaluation.native_execution_wall_hours: about 7.5 (2 models x 300 x 8 x 2 revisions x 45 s / 16)
one_time_evaluation.atheris_wall_hours: about 19 (2 modes x 300 targets x 600 CPU-s x 3 seeds / 16)

repository_native.smaller_alternative: at N=200 the CPU totals scale by about two thirds; power is lower (see the power analysis)

blockers.blocker: no candidate data exists locally; mining needs network access and a licence review
WSL lacks Python 3.10/3.13 and any hash-locking environment tool (uv or pip-tools); Docker/Podman absent
blockers.resolution: approve installing uv in WSL (D6) or restrict to projects supporting 3.8/3.9/3.11/3.12

blockers.blocker: native execution of generated tests has never been demonstrated; official-test reproduction was 3/5 with 40% infrastructure failure
blockers.resolution: the dress rehearsal must reach a predeclared reliability (>= 90% of qualified targets execute on both revisions) before the one-time run

blockers.blocker: the Atheris adapter handles only primitives in fixed ranges; repository functions take objects and state
blockers.resolution: adapter extension and per-target reachability reporting, implemented and tested on the rehearsal pool

blockers.blocker: repository prompts are capped at 2,048 tokens and compaction may drop context
blockers.resolution: record compaction per target; exclude targets whose required buggy-side context cannot fit without dropping the target code

blockers.blocker: the consumed test split can never be read, so disjointness from it is ENFORCED only through complete indexing of the upstream sources that fed every split (coverage audit and hash-bound receipt), not by inspecting the split
blockers.resolution: user acceptance of this enforcement method (D7)

blockers.blocker: no untouched train-derived panel remains for the sampling study
blockers.resolution: accept the 613-record panel with a fresh seed family as exploratory (D8) or skip the study

blockers.blocker: the power analysis recommends N=300 (minimum 200), which needs roughly 2,000-4,300 mined candidates and about 35-40 CPU-hours

required_user_decisions.decision: approve network mining of GitHub repositories and the temporal rule (fixes on or after 2025-01-01)
confirm the admitted licence list and whether same-organisation repositories are excluded
final size: recommended N=300, minimum 200 (power analysis), with the 8% per-repository cap; the +5 pp gate is unchanged
who seals the one-time set and whether it becomes the project's new locked evaluation
Atheris: ordinary crash/contract mode as the primary paired comparison on the jointly eligible set; differential mode as a labelled upper bound; 600 CPU-s x 3 seeds per target and mode
permission to install uv (hash-locked resolution and sync) and interpreters 3.10/3.13 inside WSL
accept that disjointness is enforced against the complete indexed source universe (coverage audit + hash-bound receipt), which does not require reading any protected split
run, defer or skip the optional sampling-budget study, and its panel
which models enter the one-time evaluation (base and frozen control proposed)
